hero.heading: What this component does
hero.description: A single destination in a Navigation Rail, shown as a glyph in a square target or, in the wide form, a glyph and label on one row. It is the content the rail's Menu and Footer slots are built around, and the rail sets nothing on it beyond visibility, so every property here is yours per instance. Selection recolours the glyph and label rather than laying a scrim behind them, which is what keeps it distinct from hover and press.

rows.Description: The resting destination.
Documents the pointer-over treatment. The implementation drives this, so choosing it in a layout freezes the item in a state it should not be in.
Documents the pointer-down treatment, with the same caveat as hover.

The destination the user is currently on. It is the only state that recolours the glyph and label instead of laying a scrim behind them, so it stays legible whatever the rail sits on. Exactly one item across the rail should carry it.
The destination can be selected.
The destination is unavailable, and nothing on the item explains why. Offered on the resting state only, so an item cannot be shown selected and disabled at once.
The narrow form, a glyph in a square target with the caption hidden unless Show Label is on.
The wide form, glyph and label side by side on a single row. This should match the rail the item sits in, since the rail sets its own width independently.
The destination's name. It always shows in the wide form, and in the narrow form only when Show Label is on, where the column is too narrow for anything but a very short word.
Glyph only in the narrow form.
Adds the caption under the glyph in the narrow form. It has no effect in the wide form, where the label shows regardless.
Shows the glyph.
Hides it. In the narrow form with Show Label off this leaves an empty target with nothing to read, so only turn it off in the wide form.
No badge on the glyph.
Reveals a notification dot over the glyph's top-right corner. It sits outside the layout, so turning it on never changes the item's size or shifts its neighbours.

rows.What changes: A fully transparent ghost background, with glyph and label on interactive/neutral/foreground/default.
The ghost background rises to 5 percent opacity. Glyph and label do not change, so the scrim alone carries the feedback.
The same scrim at 10 percent. Glyph and label still do not change.
No scrim at all. The glyph and label move to interactive/subtle/foreground/default instead, which is what separates selection from hover and press.
The background fill is dropped entirely and glyph and label move to interactive/subtle/foreground/disabled.
There is no focus variant. Keyboard focus has to be rendered by the implementation.

rows.Description: Figma stores no timing and no transition is modelled. Every state change is colour or opacity only, with no movement, scale or elevation.
The badge is positioned absolutely over the glyph and sits outside the layout, so showing or hiding it never reflows the item or the rail.
Switching Expanded changes the layout direction, the padding and the text style all at once. It is a different shape rather than a resize, so it is set by the rail rather than animated.
The destination's name. There is no truncation and no wrapping, so in the narrow form a long word simply overflows its column.

The item pins Icon to Size=small with Framed off and leaves the instance exposed, so the glyph can be swapped per instance while the sizing stays consistent. See the Icon Metadata frame. It arrives holding Star, a placeholder rather than a real destination glyph.

rows.Type: nested Notification Indicator, toggled by Show Badge
rows.Description: Pinned to Size=small, the dot with no number. The item does not leave this instance exposed, so its value and size cannot be changed without detaching. At this size the dot signals that something is waiting, not how much.

sections.title: Anatomy
rawTextContent: The outer frame. Vertical and hugging in the narrow form, horizontal and fixed-width in the wide one, with a minimum on both axes so the target never shrinks below it.
The box holding the glyph, and the anchor the badge is positioned against. It does not clip, which is what lets the badge overhang its corner.
The destination's name. Hidden by default in the narrow form and always shown in the wide one, with a different text style in each.

sections.title: How to use
dos: Set exactly one item across the whole rail to selected. Selection is the item's job and neither the rail nor the panel manages it.
Swap the glyph on every item. It ships holding a Star placeholder, which says nothing about where the destination goes.
donts: Don't turn Show Icon off in the narrow form. With the caption hidden too, the item becomes an empty target with nothing to read.
Don't rely on Show Label to hide labels in the wide form. It only controls the narrow one, where the label is hidden by default anyway.

sections.title: Accessibility & Content Guidelines
items: In the narrow form the destination is a glyph alone unless Show Label is on. An icon is not a name, so the accessible name has to come from code.
Selection is carried by colour on the glyph and label, with no scrim, underline or indicator bar. It needs to be conveyed in code as well.
Hover and press are carried by a translucent scrim alone and leave the glyph and label unchanged, so neither reaches a keyboard or screen reader user.
There is no focus variant. Keyboard focus has to be rendered by the implementation.
Disabled is visual only and nothing on the item explains why a destination is unavailable.
The badge is a dot with no number at the size this component pins, so whatever it signals needs a text equivalent.

rows.Type: Hug in the narrow form, fixed in the wide one
rows.Description: 48px collapsed, growing only if a caption is wider. 176px expanded, fixed regardless of label length.
48px in both forms, held up by a control/lg minimum on both axes so the target never drops below it.
8px (space/sm) top and bottom in both. 4px (space/xs) left and right collapsed, 16px (space/lg) expanded.
None collapsed, where the caption sits directly under the glyph. 16px (space/lg) expanded, between glyph and label.
radius/sm on every variant.
A 16px Icon at Size=small with Framed off, in a 16px box that does not clip its content.
An 8px Notification Indicator at Size=small, placed at 12,-4 against the 16px glyph box so it overhangs the top-right corner, outside the layout flow.
indicator/small (10/12, Regular) collapsed, label/medium (14/20, Medium) expanded.

interactive/neutral/foreground/default at rest, hover and press. interactive/subtle/foreground/default when selected, interactive/subtle/foreground/disabled when disabled. Backgrounds come from the interactive/ghost family. Glyph and label take the same token in every state.
